name: Gibraltar
title: Category 2 Individual — assessable income cap and minimum/maximum tax
quote_original: their gross assessable income is capped at £118,000 per annum
instrument: Qualifying (Category 2) Individuals Rules 2004 (LN.2004/070), as applied by the Gibraltar Income Tax Office
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. Same page also gives minimum annual tax £37,000 and maximum £42,380, and states Category 2 individuals can only be taxed under the allowances based system. The tax treatment is the substance of this route, not an investment threshold.

name: Gibraltar
title: HEPSS — assessable income cap and fixed tax liability
quote_original: their gross assessable income is capped at £160,000 per annum
instrument: High Executive Possessing Specialist Skills Rules 2008 (LN.2008/016), as applied by the Gibraltar Income Tax Office
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. Same page states the annual total tax liability would be £39,940 and that HEPSS holders can only be taxed under the Gross Income Based system. The page does NOT state the HEPSS minimum salary requirement or the accommodation requirement — those were not verified by me on an official page.

name: Gibraltar
title: Category 2 — immigration permission is discretionary under s.19(C)
quote_original: Individuals will need to apply for discretionary permission to reside in Gibraltar.
instrument: Immigration, Asylum and Refugee Act, section 19(C)
notes: PDF fetched 2026-07-30 and read with pdftotext -layout; quote is from the 'Non EU Nationals who qualify for residency' section under Category 2 Individuals. The same paragraph names section 19(C) of the Immigration, Asylum & Refugee Act as the permission-to-reside power. This matters for the atlas: Category 2 is a TAX status, and residence for a non-EU national is a separate discretionary grant, not a right. Whitespace in the PDF text layer may differ from a re-fetch — the quote above is a single contiguous sentence in the extracted text.

name: Gibraltar
title: Category 2 — June 2026 net wealth and fee reform
instrument: HMGoG press release 469/2026, 18 June 2026; amending instrument not identified
notes: How far I got: I fetched this press release on 2026-07-30 and read a summary of it — minimum net wealth for NEW applicants raised from £2 million to £5 million, application fee raised from £1,233 to £5,000, existing Category 2 individuals fully grandfathered, loss of Category 2 status ends the right to reside, no access to publicly funded schooling or healthcare. I did NOT capture verbatim text, so quote_original is deliberately empty rather than reconstructed. NEXT STEP: re-fetch this URL and lift the exact sentences, then find the Legal Notice amending rule 8(1)(a) of the Qualifying (Category 2) Individuals Rules 2004 on gibraltarlaws.gov.gi and its commencement date. Note the net wealth figure appears to be an administrative policy criterion — the Rules themselves say only that the applicant must be of 'substantial and sound financial standing'. Anyone still publishing £2 million is out of date.

name: Gibraltar
title: Category 2 / HEPSS statutory detail in the consolidated Rules
instrument: Qualifying (Category 2) Individuals Rules 2004 (LN.2004/070); High Executive Possessing Specialist Skills Rules 2008 (LN.2008/016)

I did NOT personally fetch this URL, so none of that is first-hand and no quote is recorded. name: Jersey
title: High Value Residency — minimum annual tax contribution
quote_original: a minimum tax contribution of £250,000 under Article 135A of the Income Tax (Jersey) Law
instrument: Income Tax (Jersey) Law, Article 135A; Control of Housing and Work (Jersey) Law 2012
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. The route grants Entitled residential status (the 2(1)(e) category). Approval is discretionary, assessed on social or economic benefit and the best interests of the Island community, overseen by the Head of High Value Residency. Critical distinction for the atlas: 2(1)(e) is a housing-and-work status plus a tax treatment, NOT immigration leave — a non-EEA national needs separate immigration permission, which this route does not confer.

name: Jersey
title: High Value Residency — income and property thresholds
quote_original: annual worldwide earnings well above £1.25 million, guaranteed for at least 10 years
instrument: Control of Housing and Work (Jersey) Law 2012, Regulation 2(1)(e)
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. Same page gives the property purchase minimums: a house worth more than £3.5 million, or an apartment worth more than £1.75 million — the apartment tier is the lowest qualifying entry point. No minimum physical presence in days is published on this page.

name: Jersey
title: High Value Residency — tax rate bands
quote_original: the first £1.25 million is taxable at 20% and amounts above that are taxable at 1%
instrument: Income Tax (Jersey) Law, Article 135A
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. Jersey land and property income is taxable at 20% with no upper band. Where actual income falls short, the applicant is deemed to receive sufficient additional income to ensure the £250,000 minimum is paid. The £250,000 figure applies to applicants from 14 July 2023; a grandfathered pre-2018 cohort electing into the 2018 rules had £145,000, increased to £170,000 from 2023 — do not use the legacy figures as headline. From year of assessment 2026 mandatory independent taxation applies to all married couples including high value residents.

name: Isle of Man
title: Business Migrant (Innovator) — investment funds
quote_original: at least £50,000 in investment funds
instrument: Isle of Man Immigration Rules, Appendix X (Business Migrant), Part 7
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. Required for a new business; not required where the business is already established and was endorsed for an earlier visa. Team members cannot share the same funds, so £50,000 per Innovator applicant. The Department for Enterprise is the sole endorsing body. Maintenance is separate: at least £945 in the bank for 90 consecutive days before applying. English at CEFR B2 or a degree taught in English recognised by ECCTIS. Leave is 3 years, extendable by 3 with no limit on extensions.

name: Isle of Man
title: Business Migrant (Innovator) — settlement after three years
quote_original: You may be able to apply for settlement (known as 'indefinite leave to remain') once you've been in the Isle of Man for 3 years.
instrument: Isle of Man Immigration Rules, Appendix X (Business Migrant), Part 7
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. This is what qualifies the Innovator route for the atlas — it is investment-based AND leads to settlement. The Isle of Man runs its own immigration control with its own Rules. Note the apostrophe in 'indefinite leave to remain' is a typographic right single quote on the page; normalise before matching if a re-fetch differs.

name: Isle of Man
title: Business Migrant (Start-up) — no extension, no settlement
quote_original: You cannot extend this visa.
instrument: Isle of Man Immigration Rules, Appendix X (Business Migrant), Part 6
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. Leave is 2 years 4 months, capped at 2 years total across all approvals; the page states applicants cannot settle in the UK on this visa, so the route does not itself lead to settlement — the intended progression is to switch into Innovator. No investment funds requirement is stated for Start-up. Maintenance £945 for 90 consecutive days; English at CEFR B2 or an equivalent degree. Department for Enterprise is the only endorsing body.

name: Isle of Man
title: Worker Migrant five-year settlement and Long Residence settlement
instrument: Isle of Man Immigration Rules in effect from 24 July 2026 (SD 62/05 as amended), Appendix W Part 2 and Appendix Long Residence
notes: How far I got: I confirmed on https://www.gov.im/categories/travel-traffic-and-motoring/immigration/settle/ that a settlement category exists, but that page did not detail qualifying periods for Worker Migrant or a long residence route. A delegated research pass reported reading this Rules PDF and reported Appendix W para 2.4(2) requiring 'a continuous period of 5 years lawfully in the Isle of Man, of which the most recent period must have been spent with permission as a Worker Migrant', a salary floor of the higher of £25,447.50 per annum or the going rate from 31 October 2025, a 180-day absence cap per 12-month period, and Appendix Long Residence requiring a 10-year qualifying period. I did NOT personally fetch the PDF, so no quote is recorded. NEXT STEP: fetch this PDF (confirm it is still the current version — the Rules are reissued frequently) and lift verbatim text for Appendix W para 2.4(2) and Appendix Long Residence LR 3.1. Note the Worker Migrant route is employer-sponsored and is only in scope for this atlas BECAUSE it leads to settlement.

name: Fiji
title: Investor Permit — statutory basis
quote_original: Section 9(2)(c) of the Immigration Act, 2003
instrument: Immigration Act 2003, s.9(2)(c)
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. The permit is granted to non-citizen investors engaged in a business project approved by the Fiji Islands Trade and Investment Bureau, via a Foreign Investment Certificate. IMPORTANT GAP: this official page publishes NO minimum investment amount, no permit duration options and no fees. The widely quoted FJD 250,000 and FJD 500,000 figures do not appear on it.

name: Fiji
title: Three-year Investor Permit under the Immigration Regulations
quote_original: A Three (3) Years Investor Permit is issued to foreign investors who are able to show proof of funds remitted from offshore and injected into the local economy
instrument: Immigration Regulations 2007, regulation 39
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. The page is internally inconsistent and this should be flagged: it is TITLED 'Seven (7) Years Investor Permit' but its body describes only the three-year permit and gives no detail on a seven-year tier. The page cites Section 39 of the Immigration Regulation 2007 and publishes no monetary amount.

name: Fiji
title: Seven-year Investor Permit — FJD 250,000 threshold
instrument: Immigration Regulations 2007 (LN 5 of 2008), regulation 41(2)-(3)
notes: How far I got: no official Fiji page I fetched publishes an investor threshold. A delegated research pass reported that regulation 41(3) requires the foreign investor to 'undertake to invest and maintain in a business an amount of not less than $250,000 or such other amount as the Minister may, from time to time, determine' for a seven-year ministerial permit, but reported reading that text from a third-party mirror because laws.gov.fj would not serve the instrument. I did not personally verify it. NEXT STEP: obtain the official consolidated text of the Immigration Regulations 2007 from laws.gov.fj or the Fiji Government Gazette and quote reg 41(2)-(3) verbatim; also establish whether the Minister has since determined a different amount. Separately, clarify whether the commonly cited FJD 250,000 is an immigration-law threshold or the foreign investment registration threshold under the Investment Act 2021 administered by Investment Fiji — these are different things and are routinely conflated. The FJD 500,000 figure appears in neither and should be treated as unsupported.

name: Fiji
title: Residence on Assured Income Permit — Fiji's retirement route
quote_original: The principal applicants spouse and dependent children can be included in the same form
instrument: Immigration Regulations 2007, regulations 48-50
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. Sic — the page omits the apostrophe in 'applicants'. Other detail on the page: applications must be made by persons 45 years and above; the applicant must have assets outside Fiji sufficient to ensure they will not become a charge on public funds; new applicants supply a latest offshore bank statement in Fijian currency, extensions a local one; fee FJD 650.05 for both new and extension; standard processing 21 working days. IMPORTANT GAP: NO minimum asset or income figure is published. The commonly quoted FJD 100,000 transfer into a Fiji bank account appears nowhere on the official page — treat it as unsupported. The page also does not state duration, renewal terms, statutory basis or whether it leads to permanent residence.

name: Honduras
title: Rentista — USD 2,500 monthly income requirement (statute text)
quote_original: DOS MIL QUINIENTOS DÓLARES
instrument: Ley de Migración y Extranjería (Decreto Legislativo No. 208-2003), artículo 23
notes: PDF fetched 2026-07-30 and read with pdftotext -layout. This is a scan of La Gaceta, Diario Oficial No. 36,924 of Saturday 23 August 2025, hosted by UNAH's OMIH observatory. Article 23 is quoted verbatim in footnote 1 of the Acuerdo: rentista income must be permanent, lawful and stable, generated abroad or in national territory, 'no menores de DOS MIL QUINIENTOS DÓLARES (USD $ 2,500.00l) mensuales' — note the gazette itself contains a stray 'l' typo after the figure, so a longer quote will not match cleanly; the short quote above is safe. NEXT STEP if a cleaner citation is wanted: locate an ENAG or gob.hn hosted copy of La Gaceta No. 36,924 rather than the university mirror.

name: Honduras
title: Pensionado — USD 1,500 monthly pension requirement (statute text)
quote_original: MIL QUINIENTOS DÓLARES (USD $ 1,500,00) mensuales
instrument: Ley de Migración y Extranjería (Decreto Legislativo No. 208-2003), artículo 24
notes: Same gazette PDF, footnote 2, fetched 2026-07-30. Article 24 requires permanent and stable pensions 'generadas o provenientes del exterior' — unlike rentista, the pension must originate abroad. The gazette prints the figure with a comma as '1,500,00'; the quote above reproduces that exactly.

name: Honduras
title: Inversionista — USD 50,000 minimum investment (statute text)
quote_original: MIL DOLARES DE LOS ESTADOS UNIDOS DE AMÉRICA ($50,000) o su
instrument: Ley de Migración y Extranjería (Decreto Legislativo No. 208-2003), artículo 33 numeral 2
notes: Same gazette PDF, footnote 3, fetched 2026-07-30. Full sentence across a line break reads 'La inversión será por un mínimo de CINCUENTA MIL DOLARES DE LOS ESTADOS UNIDOS DE AMÉRICA ($50,000) o su equivalente en moneda nacional'; the quote above is the contiguous single line to survive a re-fetch. Note the gazette spells DOLARES without the accent here.

name: Honduras
title: Acuerdo 374-2025 — discretionary residence at 50% of thresholds
quote_original: deberán comprobar que cuentan con al menos el 50%
instrument: Acuerdo Ministerial No. 374-2025, La Gaceta No. 36,924, 23 August 2025; implementing artículo 21 numeral 8 of the Ley de Migración y Extranjería
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. PRIMERO opens four gateways to article 21(8) exceptional residence: (1) applicants failing the essential requirements of the qualities in article 21 numerals 1-5, who must still file that quality's documents and fee, and where the shortfall is the money, must show at least 50% of what rentista, pensionado or inversionista requires; (2) holders of permits for up to 5 years who broke continuity; (3) people working in the country with at least 2 years continuous legal residence, work authorisation from the Secretaría de Trabajo y Previsión Social or the INM, and employer certification under article 11 of the Código del Trabajo (90% of employees and 85% of payroll to Hondurans); (4) other cases with at least 120 days continuous legal residence justified on humanitarian, public interest or special family grounds. The Acuerdo states the 50% RULE and does not name derived figures — USD 1,250 rentista, USD 750 pensionado, USD 25,000 investment are arithmetic, not quotations. The grant is fully discretionary: it is subject to the 'análisis, valoración y criterio exclusivo' of the SGJD, which reserves the right to accept, deny or archive without creating any acquired right. QUINTO makes it effective from the date of the Acuerdo; SGJD's official communiqué dates the lineamientos from 30 July 2025.

name: Honduras
title: Rentista — official requirement sheet and fee
quote_original: Acreditar tarifa de $300.00
instrument: Secretaría de Gobernación, Justicia y Descentralización — Requisitos para obtener residencia como rentista
notes: PDF fetched 2026-07-30 and read with pdftotext -layout. The same sheet requires the applicant to prove income 'no menores de $2,500.00 mensuales o su equivalente en moneda nacional', and a certificate showing assets, securities or other income-generating means with the income received through an institution of the Sistema Financiero Nacional. Other requirements: application addressed to the Secretario de Estado en los Despachos de Derechos Humanos, Justicia, Gobernación y Descentralización; migratory movement certification from the INM; consular entry application (waived if already in Honduras); criminal record certificates from country of origin and last residence; DPI certification; medical certification. This independently corroborates the statutory figure on a second official domain.

name: Honduras
title: Reglamento detail and Residente Inmigrado permanent residence
instrument: Reglamento de la Ley de Migración y Extranjería, artículos 23, 25, 31-33, 39-40, 84-85
notes: How far I got: I verified the primary statute figures and the Acuerdo myself, but not the Reglamento. A delegated research pass reported reading the Reglamento at this Tribunal Superior de Cuentas library URL and reported: article 23 barring rentistas from salaried work while permitting investment; article 30 allowing investment above the inversionista thresholds without changing migratory quality; articles 27-29 granting customs franchises and exempting foreign-source income; article 84 issuing the carné de residencia for up to five years and article 85 requiring proof on renewal that the income continues; article 39 setting four cumulative conditions for residente inmigrado including 'Haber permanecido en el país por un período no menor de cinco años consecutivos'; and nationality-tiered fees of USD 300 Central American, USD 400 Ibero-American, USD 500 other. I did not personally fetch it. NEXT STEP: fetch this URL and quote articles 39 and 84-85 verbatim. name: Finland
title: Start-up entrepreneur permit — 2026 income requirement
quote_original: your net income must be at least EUR 1,210 / 1,090 / 1,030 per month, depending on where you live
instrument: Ulkomaalaislaki (Aliens Act) 301/2004, s.80 (kasvuyrittäjän oleskelulupa)
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. Three-tier regional figure for 2026; EUR 1,030 is the lowest tier. Requires a Business Finland eligibility statement before applying — only one person in the start-up team needs to apply for the statement. No minimum investment or capital figure is stated; the applicant must show sufficient financial resources for the whole permit period, in their own account. First permit up to 2 years, extensions up to 4 years. Fees: EUR 650 electronic first permit, EUR 230 electronic extension, EUR 800 paper first, EUR 430 paper extension. Fast-track processing available in as little as two weeks. The page does not state the Aliens Act section or the A/B permit type — those were not verified by me.

name: Finland
title: Permanent residence — pre-8-January-2026 qualifying period
quote_original: a continuous period of 4 years with a continuous residence permit (A permit)
instrument: Ulkomaalaislaki (Aliens Act) 301/2004, s.56, as amended with effect from 8 January 2026
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. MATERIAL CHANGE — the quoted 4-year rule applies only to applications submitted BEFORE 8 January 2026. For applications on or after that date the requirement varies by pathway: standard 6 years, high income 4 years, advanced degree 4 years. A new Finnish or Swedish language requirement also applies, ranging from developing (A2) to particularly good (C1) depending on pathway, with applicants aged 65 and over potentially exempt. Do not publish the flat 4-year rule as current. NOT VERIFIED BY ME: the number of the amending act, and the income figure defining the high income pathway.

name: Finland
title: Entrepreneur / self-employed permit — profitability test
quote_original: Your business must be profitable.
instrument: Ulkomaalaislaki (Aliens Act) 301/2004, s.79 (yrittäjän oleskelulupa)
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. The Economic Development Centre (elinvoimakeskus.fi, which replaced the ELY Centres) issues a partial decision first, then Migri decides. Means of support must be secured by income from the business. IMPORTANT GAP: no monthly euro figure is published on this page — do not borrow the start-up entrepreneur tiers. Fees 2026: EUR 750 electronic first permit, EUR 230 electronic extension, EUR 900 paper first, EUR 430 paper extension. First permits are applied for from abroad, extensions from within Finland. The page does not state A or B permit type or duration. This is the permit Migri points remote workers to; it requires a genuine Finland-based business, not remote work for a foreign employer.

name: Lithuania
title: Startup visa, company-owner and investment-agreement routes
instrument: Law on the Legal Status of Aliens No. IX-2206, arts. 40, 44-1, 45, 45-1, 49-5, 53; Law on Investments No. VIII-1312, arts. 13-1, 15-7
notes: How far I got: I established that www.migracija.lt is an Angular single-page app that serves no content to a plain fetch, so departmental guidance could not be read directly; official mirrors migracija.lrv.lt, osp.stat.gov.lt and uzt.lt were reported returning HTTP 403, and startupvisa.lt did not resolve. A delegated research pass reported reading the consolidated statute at this URL (version in force 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31) and reported: art. 45-1 startup visa with a maximum of 4 foreign participants, 2 years renewable for 3, gated on a written confirmation from the institution authorised by the Minister of Economy and Innovation, with NO capital or job-creation threshold; art. 45(1)(1) company owner requiring 6 months of prior activity, equity of at least EUR 28,000 of which at least EUR 14,000 is the applicant's own, a payroll of at least 2x the average monthly gross wage, and manager status or a 1/3 shareholding; art. 45(1)(2-1) requiring EUR 260,000 invested and five local jobs, for 3 years; art. 45(1)(2-2) requiring EUR 500,000 company equity and ten local jobs, a management rather than personal-investment route; Investment Law art. 13-1(3) allowing a permit for an investor or a participant owning at least 1/10 of share capital with at least EUR 14,000 invested under a signed state investment agreement, gated on the investor having had EUR 2.5 million annual revenue; art. 15-7(5) major-project route; art. 49-5 nationality-based route for citizens of Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, the UK and the USA that uniquely admits plain self-employment; and art. 53 permanent residence after 5 uninterrupted years with state language and Constitution exams. I did NOT personally fetch any of this. NEXT STEP: fetch this URL and the Investment Law at https://e-seimas.lrs.lt/portal/legalAct/lt/TAD/TAIS.84573/asr and quote the article text verbatim in Lithuanian, taking care with diacritics. Also unresolved: the current euro value of the average monthly gross wage (BDU) benchmark that the payroll and Blue Card multipliers depend on — three mutually inconsistent values were seen in secondary sources and none was confirmed on an official page.

name: Kyrgyzstan
title: Residence permit categories and the 2024 digital nomad amendment
instrument: Law of the Kyrgyz Republic on External Labour Migration (Закон КР «О внешней трудовой миграции»), amendments reportedly signed 9 October 2024

Until an official source is found, Kyrgyzstan should carry no route rows.

name: Malawi
title: Business Residence Permit — USD 50,000 and source of funds
quote_original: The funds to be invested should originate from a legal source outside
instrument: Immigration Act (Cap 15:03) and Immigration Regulations — specific section not cited on the page
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. Sic — the sentence on the page ends without naming Malawi. Minimum investment USD 50,000.00. Open to foreign nationals investing in manufacturing, mining, agriculture, fisheries, tourism, financial services or other productive sectors. Valid 5 years from date of approval, renewable for successive 5-year periods; renewal must be applied for 3 months before expiry. Applications are submitted at Immigration Headquarters or Regional Immigration Offices and go to the Minister for decision, so the grant is discretionary. Fees are due within 30 days of approval. IMPORTANT GAPS: the page does not itemise fees and does not cite Immigration Act sections or Regulations class numbers. A USD 800 issuance fee circulates in secondary sources and is NOT on this page — treat as unsupported.

name: Malawi
title: Permanent Residence Permit — five years ordinary residence
quote_original: any person who has been ordinarily resident in Malawi for a period not less than five years
instrument: Immigration Act (Cap 15:03) and Immigration Regulations — specific section not cited on the page
notes: Fetched 2026-07-30. The full eligibility sentence also covers foreign nationals wishing to reside in Malawi permanently, foreign wives of Malawians, over-aged dependants of Permanent Resident Permit holders, and — relevant to a retirement route — 'elderly people who would wishes to spend their life after retirement in Malawi, (people of assured income)', sic including the grammatical error. That retirement gateway carries NO published income threshold, so no figure should be recorded for it. Decided by the Minister; applications at Immigration Headquarters or Regional offices; fees due within 30 days of approval notification, amounts not published. The page cites no Immigration Act sections. NOT VERIFIED: whether Business Residence Permit time counts toward the five years, and the naturalisation link.
